facts.raw_span: intensely pruritic skin eruption
appeared approximately 24 hours after intensive sun exposure
episode of malaise and headache 2 weeks before first presentation
no history of photosensitivity
denied the use of any topical or systemic photosensitizers
Erythema and helical thickening as well as numerous small blisters, 2 to 3 mm in diameter, were present on both ears
numerous small blisters, 2 to 3 mm in diameter
Differential blood count, routine chemical analysis, and serum porphyrins were unremarkable
Serum parvovirus B19 (PVB19) IgM and IgG antibodies were detectable
PVB19 DNA was found (viral load of 0.2 PVB19 DNA copies/β-globin gene copy, or 33,438 copies/μg of isolated DNA) in lesional skin biopsy specimen

Negative results for herpes simplex viruses 1 and 2, varicella zoster virus, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, human herpesvirus 6, hepatitis B and C viruses, 8 human polyomaviruses, and enteroviruses
Standard phototesting with UV-A and UV-B was unremarkable

concepts.why: The presence of serum parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibodies and PVB19 DNA in lesional skin biopsy specimen supports this diagnosis.
The temporal relationship between sun exposure and the onset of the skin eruption, along with the presence of erythema and blisters, suggests this diagnosis.
The appearance of the skin eruption after sun exposure is consistent with this diagnosis, although the lack of response to phototesting reduces its likelihood.

The intensely pruritic skin eruption and the presence of erythema and blisters could be consistent with this diagnosis, although the absence of a characteristic herald patch and the presence of PVB19 DNA make it less likely.

The episode of malaise and headache 2 weeks before the skin eruption, along with the detection of PVB19 antibodies, suggests a viral etiology, but this is a broader category and less specific than the other options.

rationales.F01: The presence of an intensely pruritic skin eruption is more typical of Erythema infectiosum and viral exanthem.
rationales.F02: The appearance of the eruption after sun exposure is more typical of Sun-induced erythema multiforme and Polymorphic light eruption.
rationales.F03: The episode of malaise and headache 2 weeks before presentation is more typical of Erythema infectiosum and viral exanthem.
rationales.F09: The presence of Serum parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibodies is highly suggestive of Erythema infectiosum.
rationales.F10: The presence of PVB19 DNA in lesional skin biopsy specimen is highly suggestive of Erythema infectiosum.

frontier_selector.rationale: Detection of PVB19 DNA in lesional skin biopsy and presence of PVB19 IgM and IgG antibodies support Erythema infectiosum diagnosis
